clue.text: Alarming detectives with hose crushing resistance

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector; plural gives DIS

indicators.note: something crushing another presses round it, so one piece closes about the other

parts.note: a hose is flexible tubing
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Police officers wielding a hosepipe to quell protesters make for an alarming sight.
explanation.walkthrough: DI, a detective inspector, is the usual crossword detective; 'crushing' has the hose squeezing the resistance inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disturbing causes worry or unease, which is what an alarming thing does too.

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means tipped over, so the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a tad is a small amount

explanation.surface: Someone is somewhat put out on receiving secret information.
explanation.walkthrough: A TAD, read upwards, spells DATA.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence in the military or spying sense is gathered information, which is data.

clue.text: Excessive load put daily into stream

indicators.note: one thing placed into another ends up inside it

parts.note: a surge is a rushing stream or flow
a daily, or char, is a cleaning lady who comes in every day

explanation.surface: Too much weight is being dumped in a river every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like an adverb but is the British noun for a cleaner, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an extra or excessive load, used of both charges and physical weight.

clue.text: Body, perhaps where body is found?

definitions.text: Body, perhaps where body is found?

parts.words: Body, perhaps where body is found?
parts.note: surface reading: a detective wondering where a corpse might be discovered
setter's reading: a body is a one-piece garment, an example of intimate wear, and it is worn right next to the body beneath the outer garments

explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Body' is a garment (a bodysuit); the second is a person's body, which lies beneath its covering of dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A body, or bodysuit, is an item of lingerie, so it is an example of the garments worn beneath outer dress.

indicators.note: one item placed inside another sits within it

parts.note: rubbish is kept in bins
food gone rancid is off

explanation.surface: Clever people find something rotten in the dustbins.
explanation.walkthrough: Boffin is British slang for a scientist or expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Brains is informal for clever people, and boffins are scientists or experts.

clue.text: Good person in zero alcohol panacea

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: zero means none, no
a saint is a good person, abbreviated ST
rum is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A virtuous teetotaller promotes a cure-all for every ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zero alcohol' must be read as the phrase 'no rum', with the saint slipped inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack remedy claimed to cure everything, which is what a panacea is.

indicators.note: the words hold the solution within them, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the last letters of the first word run into the first of the second

explanation.surface: A tin holds some rock-derived powder.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft magnesium silicate mineral, ground for talcum powder.

indicators.note: first off tells you to drop the opening letter

parts.note: something damaged has been harmed

explanation.surface: Someone hurt, to begin with, is now carrying weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First off' reads as 'to begin with' but instructs you to remove the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed means equipped with guns or other arms.

parts.note: a con is a convict
to troll is to post abuse online

explanation.surface: An offender who was harassing people online is now being held back.
explanation.walkthrough: Trolling is posting deliberately abusive or provocative messages on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Controlled means held in check, kept under restraint.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a drawn game is tied
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Someone looks exhausted and haggard after a run-in with a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' suggests a haggard face, but it means level at the end of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Drained of energy means exhausted, the same as tired.

parts.note: surface reading: a musician who plays the bass guitar or double bass
setter's reading: bass is also a sea fish, and someone who angles for it plays it on the line

explanation.walkthrough: Bass rhymes with 'face' as an instrument but with 'mass' as a fish; an angler plays a hooked fish to tire it.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler plays a hooked bass on the line, so someone who catches fish for sport or a living fits.

parts.note: to enter data is to record it

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a taint is a stain or smear
blokes is British slang for men

explanation.surface: A recorded show smears the men involved.
explanation.walkthrough: To record data in a ledger or log is to enter it; the blokes go inside the smear just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance is a show put on to amuse an audience, a piece of entertainment.

clue.text: It's tougher accepting one is stouter

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: 'it's tougher' is 'it's harder'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Taking on one more makes things harder for a heavier person.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout can mean sturdy and robust, so stouter means more robust, hardier.

clue.text: Throne under dynasty of rulers, initially

definitions.text: Throne under dynasty of rulers, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word before it

parts.note: the first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A royal house that sat on the English throne at the start of a line of monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the Tudors held the English throne as a ruling dynasty from 1485 to 1603.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the royal house of Henry VII to Elizabeth I, a dynasty of English monarchs.

clue.text: See saint wearing majestic old crown

indicators.note: something wearing a garment is covered by it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: epic means grand and majestic
S is the abbreviation for saint
O is a standard abbreviation for old
the pate is the crown of the head

explanation.surface: Look at a saint dressed in a splendid antique crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is the noun for a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's office or jurisdiction, and episcopate means the office of bishop.

indicators.note: one word placed around another encloses it

parts.note: proles is short for the proletariat, working people
A is an abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: Ordinary Americans are let out of prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Releases is a noun here, as is the answer, both plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Paroles are conditional early discharges from prison, a kind of release.

clue.text: Twin regularly rejected in warlike wedding

definitions.note: wedding is a noun used attributively (wedding vows) while marital is an adjective

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the kept letters run backwards
in places the turned pair into the next word, where it takes the place of the same pair the right way round
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first and third letters
martial means relating to war

explanation.surface: One twin is cast out from a stormy, combative wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The warlike word already holds the two letters taken from 'Twin'; turning that pair round where it sits makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital means relating to marriage, as in a wedding ring or wedding vows.

clue.text: Staff organise church in time period

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to run an event is to organise it
CH is the abbreviation for church
an eon is a vast period of time

explanation.surface: Employees arrange church services over a period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees but means a stick; 'time period' splits into two abbreviations that wrap the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short club carried by police, and a staff is a stick or rod.

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the words before it go after the word that comes next

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
wee is Scottish for little
a tie is a bond such as friendship

explanation.surface: A small friendship develops after a second romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Wee is Scottish and northern English for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Love and sweetie are both affectionate terms of address for a loved one.

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to act is to pretend

explanation.surface: A former spouse is said to have been faking a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand and obtain, so exacted means claimed as due.

clue.text: Bust, possibly, is about right size

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders, a kind of statue
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A tailor's remark that a bust measurement is about the right size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' suggests a chest measurement, but it is a sculpture, of which statue is the broader class.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature means height or physical size of a person.

indicators.note: overturning in a down clue flips the words so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd
as means like
A1 means first-class, written AI with the digit as letter I

explanation.surface: An odd tale of a leading fighter being overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'Strange, like' is overturned; A1, meaning first-rate, is written with the digit as a letter I in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a member of Japan's hereditary military class, a warrior.

clue.text: Books au pair occasionally for animal

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the even-numbered letters

explanation.surface: A family books a live-in nanny now and then to mind a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest mammal of central Africa related to the giraffe.

indicators.note: endless means losing the tail, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ultimately means at last

explanation.surface: The deity is finally everlasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas is the Titan of Greek myth condemned to hold up the heavens.

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the solution is a portion of the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A man who has achieved something once a year.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition word also starts the letters that hold the solution, a double duty some setters allow.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a calendar or reference book published yearly, so it is an annual.

parts.note: I is one, with the 's
L is the abbreviation for left
read as sweet-heart, the heart or middle letter of sweet

explanation.surface: A man, perhaps, has walked out on his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea; 'sweetheart' splits into sweet and heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, an example of an isle; 'say' marks the example.

clue.text: Roll reptile over eating large reptile

indicators.note: over means turned back, so the pair reads right to left

parts.note: a rota is a roll or list of duties

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside

parts.note: the gila is a venomous American lizard
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: One reptile rolls over to devour a big one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reptile' appears twice: the first is the wordplay's gila, the last the definition. ROTA GILA reads backwards as ALIGATOR, which then takes in L.
explanation.definitionFit: The alligator is a large crocodilian reptile of America and China.

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: even so means nevertheless
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone gives up all the same, with no affection left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quits' looks like a verb but is the adjective of being square with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits means neither owes the other, which is being evens.

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, with the 's
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A claim that the monarch's form of speech is proper English.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Entry in a ball holding hand

indicators.note: holding means gripping, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: a ball is a dance
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Getting into a dance while holding someone's hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball' is a formal dance, not something you hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Admittance is the right or act of entering a place, the same as entry.
